analysis.title: Inflation-linked Weekly: Political interference at every corner (10 November 2026)
key_insights: Energy prices fell sharply in the week to 10 Nov, with Brent down EUR25/bl and TTF gas down EUR12/MWh. The bank cites de-escalation with Iran after the Democratic midterm win and talks with Qatar. A new surge stays possible until the Strait of Hormuz is settled.

The bank cut its November Eurozone headline HICP forecast to 3.71% YoY from 3.95%, versus 4.00% in October. It lowered its Eurozone core forecast by about 10bp to 2.9% for 2027 and by 3-4bp to 2.3% for 2028.

October flash Eurozone core HICP was 2.54% YoY (2.50% in September), 6bp above the bank's own estimate. The upside came mainly from tourism-related services such as accommodation and airfares, which could partly reverse. Core goods rose only 2bp.

Producer prices show little spillover from the energy shock to consumer goods. Manufacturing PPI rose to 7.0% YoY in September from 0.3% in February, while consumer goods PPI was 0.4%. The bank still expects food and furnishings inflation to pick up.

An amendment to end OATei/OATi issuance was adopted in the French National Assembly on 4 Nov. It had no effect because the whole revenue section of the 2027 budget was then rejected. The bank sees the usual 2027 issuance pattern as almost certain and expects more political interference on inflation.

The bank argues France is unlikely to copy Germany in ending linker supply. Its reasons are a programme of about EUR25bn a year, roughly EUR30bn of extra nominal OAT issuance that would be needed, the value of predictability, and the need of Livret A-distributing banks to hedge inflation. Supply would be at risk only if an RN or LFI president, a supportive Assembly, a government keeping the pledge and a permissive fiscal position all coincide.

PM Lecornu announced a Livret A ceiling increase of 10-30% on 3 Nov. The Livret A rate may rise to about 2.6% in February and 2.8% in August, which would likely bring large inflows and more demand for French inflation hedges. The bank closed its sell 3YF2Y FRCPIx vs HICPx trade at a 3bp loss.

The bank says Eurozone inflation swaps and breakevens are starting to look attractive. Its core forecasts are about 2.9% in 2027 and 2.3-2.4% in 2028, while forwards sit near 2.0%, so the market prices roughly zero inflation premium. It names energy and risk sentiment as the main drivers, with technicals and valuation turning supportive.
The open trade is sell OATei Jul-47 breakeven vs BTPei Feb-46, with P&L of about 5bp. The 2026 trade book stands at 75bp over 16 trades with a 63% hit ratio, down 4bp on the week.

Mélenchon's 2027 programme (about 15% minimum wage rise, wage indexation, price freezes on essentials) is estimated by the bank to add about 125bp to headline inflation over three years. The bank notes his probability of winning is very low on current polling.

For US CPI, the bank expects October headline at 0.29% MoM SA and core at 0.26% MoM SA, above the 0.24% Bloomberg consensus cited in the text. No YoY print is available because the October 2025 index was never published. The bank's CPI path has converged to market fixings after the oil decline.

The bank views the US midterms as not a U-turn for inflation. Crude fell from about USD110/bl to USD90/bl in two weeks on ceasefire hopes, and the bank expects gridlock on fiscal policy and no major AI regulation. It sees some local roadblocks to data centre construction.

macro_indicators.interpretation: October flash came in 3bp above the bank's estimate, with upside from energy and tourism-related services.
Up from 2.50% in September. The bank attributes the rise to volatile tourism-related services that may partly reverse.
Cut from 3.95% because of lower motor fuel, gas and electricity prices.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Lowered by about 10bp on lower gas prices easing spillover to overall inflation. The 2028 average is 2.3%.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Below September's 0.33% and August's 0.29%. The text cites a 0.24% Bloomberg consensus, while the release table shows 0.22%.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Slightly lower than last week's estimates because of lower energy prices. Together with the higher ceiling it should drive inflows and French inflation hedging demand.

macro_indicators.reading: raised from EUR22,950 to between EUR25,000 and EUR30,000

trade_ideas.description: Sell OATei Jul-47 breakeven vs BTPei Feb-46 (open, entered 1 Jun 2026 at 25.9bp, now 24.0bp)
trade_ideas.rationale: There is increasingly less justification for a premium in OATei breakeven versus BTPei, with less BTPei Feb-46 supply ahead.

risk_factors: A new surge in energy wholesale prices remains possible until the Strait of Hormuz situation is settled.
Re-escalation with Iran is possible if Trump responds to the midterm defeat with greater assertiveness.
Political interference on inflation-linked issuance in France, in particular if an RN or LFI president takes office.
Airfares could stay high for several months as airline jet fuel hedges expire, and food and furnishings inflation could exceed what PPIs suggest.
Higher Livret A ceiling and rate could change French inflation hedging demand, which is why the bank does not want to be short French inflation.
charts_described: Fig 1 compares Eurozone October YoY HICP outcomes against the CA-CIB preview, with headline 4.00% vs 3.86% (14bp upside surprise) and core 2.54% vs 2.46% (8bp), and the 14bp headline surprise mainly from energy.
Fig 8 tabulates Eurozone linker gross supply 2010-26 with 2027 estimates, including 2027 estimated total of EUR67.2bn and France at EUR23.0bn.
vol_and_positioning: The market prices roughly zero inflation premium in Eurozone inflation forwards near 2.0%, which the bank calls attractive from a contrarian perspective.
Technical supports for breakevens: a strong end-November index extension (Bonosei-27 leaving 1Y+ indices) and the usual slowdown in linker supply after 20 November.
Last week the 2YF2Y HICPx forward fell 7bp to 1.99% and the 5YF5Y fell 3.5bp to 2.07%, with the front end leading the HICPx curve lower.
geopolitical: Geopolitical de-escalation with Iran after the Democratic midterm victory, plus discussions with Qatar, cut energy prices. The Strait of Hormuz remains unsettled.
The US Chief Economist notes Trump could re-escalate with Iran in response to the midterm defeat, and that Democrats have limited ability to end the conflict alone.
Democrats won the US midterms, with governorships changing hands in Texas and Ohio. The bank expects policy gridlock, little fiscal package and local obstacles for AI data centres.

French politics: LFI and RN oppose inflation-linked bonds, and the 2027 budget will very likely pass via Article 49.3 or 47. Jean-Luc Mélenchon presented a 2027 presidential programme with wage and price measures.

tension_points.bull_case: LFI and RN lawmakers argue inflation-linked bonds have become far too costly for France as inflation rises, and the amendment to end them was initially adopted on 4 Nov.
tension_points.bear_case: CA-CIB says the programme is large, ending it would require about EUR30bn more nominal OATs, predictability matters to investors, and Livret A-distributing banks need OATi to hedge. The whole revenue section of the budget was rejected immediately.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Issuance would be at risk only if the next French president is from RN or LFI, the National Assembly backs that policy, the new government keeps the promise, and the French fiscal situation allows it.

tension_points.bull_case: With core inflation around 2.9% in 2027 and 2.3-2.4% in 2028 and forwards near 2.0%, the market prices zero inflation premium, and technicals and valuation turn supportive.
tension_points.bear_case: Energy and risk sentiment remain the main drivers, so further energy declines or weak sentiment could keep pressure on breakevens.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A new surge in energy wholesale prices is possible until the situation in the Strait of Hormuz is settled.

tension_points.theme: US inflation after midterms and Iran
tension_points.bull_case: The prospect of an Iran ceasefire looks a bit more probable, and crude has already fallen from about USD110/bl to USD90/bl.
tension_points.bear_case: The US Chief Economist notes Trump could respond to the defeat with re-escalation, which would reverse the oil decline.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Re-escalation with Iran, which would reverse the oil decline already included in the bank's energy CPI path.
